records.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:6-10 — the computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (the second overwrites the first), so minimumTokenResponseSchema actually only requires access_token; the intended "any numeric property is the expiry" validation never happens, so sync responses missing the expiry pass validation and propagate undefined expiry dates downstream.
records.rationale: The schema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`; z.string() is an object whose toString() yields "[object Object]", so both keys collapse to the same literal string and the second overwrites the first. The schema effectively only enforces access_token, so the intended expiry-validation never occurs — sync responses missing expiry pass validation. The diff shows the code verbatim in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts; mechanism verifiable.

records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:63-87 — the findFirst → update/create sequence is a check-then-act race: two concurrent webhook calls for the same (userId, appId) can both find nothing and both create, producing duplicate credentials; additionally, findFirst without orderBy is nondeterministic when duplicates already exist.
records.rationale: The new handler does `prisma.credential.findFirst` followed by a conditional `create`/`update` with no transaction or unique constraint shown, so concurrent requests for the same (userId, appId) can both pass the findFirst check and both create credentials. The diff introduces this check-then-act sequence verbatim (lines 'const appCredential = await prisma.credential.findFirst' followed by the if/else create/update), and the comment 'Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id' confirms the non-atomic approach. This is a verifiable concurrency defect in newly added code.
